memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But all the leaders answered, "We have given them our oath by the Lord, the God of Israel, and we cannot touch them now. This is what we will do to them: We will let them live, so that God's wrath will not fall on us for breaking the oath we swore to them." Then the leaders continued, "Let them live, but let them be woodcutters and water carriers in the service of the whole assembly." So the leaders' promise to them was kept. — Josh 9:19-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The leaders stand firm. Despite the people's grumbling and the fact that they had been deceived, they refuse to break their oath. "We have given them our oath by the Lord... and we cannot touch them now." They feared breaking a promise made in God's name more than they feared the inconvenience of keeping it. That is the fear of the Lord in action.

Notice their reasoning: "so that God's wrath will not fall on us for breaking the oath." They understood that how they treated their word was ultimately about how they treated God. To break a vow sworn in His name would be to treat God's name lightly. Their integrity flowed from their reverence for God Himself.

There is also wisdom in how they navigated a genuinely difficult situation. They could not break the oath, yet the Gibeonites had deceived them and there were consequences to that. So the Gibeonites were spared but given a role of service. This was not a perfect, tidy resolution, but it honoured both the promise and the seriousness of what had happened. Sometimes faithfulness means finding the honourable path through a mess we did not intend to be in.

The leaders here model something worth imitating: keeping our commitments even when we have been wronged, because our integrity is finally about our reverence for God. Jesus taught that our "yes" should simply mean yes (Matt 5:37). When we keep our word even at a cost, we honour the God whose own faithfulness never wavers, and we show a watching world what it means to belong to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is your integrity rooted in reverence for God, or merely in convenience?
2. How do you handle situations where keeping your word costs you something?
3. What does it look like to find an honourable path through a difficult situation you didn't choose?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, may my integrity flow from a deep reverence for You. Help me keep my commitments even when I have been wronged, honouring Your name in how I keep my word. Amen.
